festivals: Phalguna (Panguni) Utsavam - 10 days in Meenam (March-April), ending with Aaraattu and Pakal Pooram

history.summary: 500-year-old temple in the heart of Kottayam town, built in the 16th century by the Thekkumkoor Raja. Legend: the aging king, a devotee of Vadakkunnathan of Thrissur who could no longer make the journey, dreamed that Shiva would accompany him to Kottayam; a Shiva linga was then recovered at Samiyar Madam on the advice of a Brahmin priest from Vaikom, and the temple was built for it. The main linga is regarded as self-originated (swayambhu); the temple is counted among Kerala's 108 Sivalayas. Famed for its koothambalam (traditional theatre, regarded as one of the finest in Kerala) and for murals depicting epic stories adorning the walls.

name: Thirunakkara Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Kottayam is a city in central Kerala on the foothills of the Western Ghats, at the junction of the midland and the Kuttanad lowlands near Vembanad Lake. It is known as Kerala's 'letter capital' for its publishing industry and its rubber plantations, and is one of the state's major trading and educational centres. The Thirunakkara area lies in the heart of the city.

travel.road: Temple Road, Thirunakkara, in central Kottayam; well connected by road within the city

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; March-April during the Phalguna Utsavam festival
